title: C3276 — Power folding mirror relay
introduction:
A relay is an electrically controlled switch: a small instruction can govern another electrical circuit. For the folding mirrors, this reference maps connections described as ground, protected supply, toggle-switch input and fold or drive-position functions. I use those descriptions to understand the connections, without guessing which internal contact does the switching.

The cavity pattern is the useful little trap here: the labels do not simply march across the drawing. Start with the illustrated label, find its matching Cavity row, then read the circuit identifier, wire color, gauge, function and terminal information together. The pigtail table provides the corresponding service-part reference.

This page identifies connections; it does not teach relay access, internal switching behavior, probing, fault diagnosis or replacement. Physical viewing direction, gauge conventions and the meanings of Size and Used are not established here. Keep their printed entries as references rather than turning them into test instructions.

edits.why: The displayed face has an upper cavity, a middle row and a lower cavity. I follow the printed labels instead of assuming a familiar relay numbering pattern. The housing outline helps distinguish this layout, while the adjacent table associates it with its harness and shell; it does not establish a physical viewing side.

The Function column separates the ground, fuse-or-circuit-breaker connection, toggle-switch connection and mirror-position functions. These descriptions explain the assigned paths, not their measured state or the relay's internal contact arrangement. Read the terminal reference on each individual row because that field varies across the map.

The pigtail row links its lookup entry to a service part and engineering shell. Its gauge field contains an unexplained combined entry, which I retain without turning it into a range or assigning values to particular cavities. This table supports lookup, not replacement-wire selection or a splice procedure.
